summary: Knob Mountain steel Aermotor tower near Shickshinny, built 1921 by the state forestry department. Register says removed after 1957; newspapers name its staff through 1955.

facts.status_note: Register says removed after 1957. The latest dated entry in the sources is an April 1955 operator listing.

staffing.status: towermen and watchers named from 1922 to 1955

events.note: Erected in 1921 by the state forestry department; a September 1921 item describes the new lookout on Knob Mountain
Walter Kline appointed towerman (March 1922); Phillip Garrison fire inspector for the Nanticoke to Sunbury territory
September 1922 notice: citizens called a work day for October 9, 1922 to build an automobile road half a mile up the mountain to the tower
Bruce Henrie took up duties as watchman (October 1923)
March 1930: Mrs. Bruce Henry appointed watcher; paper believed she was the first woman to hold such a job in the state
November 1934: Emergency Relief Association set aside $8,437 for an improved road to the tower
October 1935: Frank Robbins named lookout; tower opened for the winter season
September 1936: WPA project widening the steep road to the tower
October 1947: large fire on Jackson Hill and Red Rock Mountain; about 10 acres burned; Oscar Featherman in charge at the tower
April 1955: John Falkowski listed as operator
Registered September 16, 2008, nominated by Henry Isenberg

corrections.why: The 1921 notice names the Pennsylvania Department of Forestry as the agency erecting the tower. Wyoming State Forest is the state forest where the tower stood, not an agency.

notes_for_editor: Removal date comes only from the register (after 1957); the newspaper record ends in 1955. The watchman's name is spelled Henrie in the 1923 item and Henry in the 1930 item; the story follows each. No height in sources. No source describes the site now.
